content: The Implementation Guide Toolkit Readiness Assessment Tool is designed to systematically evaluate the context in which the Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) and the Selected Practice Recommendations (SPR) will be implemented. Before proceeding with implementation, it is essential to assess the readiness and specific needs of the setting using this tool. The following steps outline the process: 1. Understand the Domains of Readiness Assessment: Familiarize yourself with the key domains that will be evaluated to determine readiness for implementation. 2. Consider the Context Using Six Categories and a Scoring System: Evaluate your specific setting by analyzing six readiness categories, assigning scores to each based on a structured scoring system. 3. Calculate Average Scores Across Team Members: Use the Readiness Scorecard to calculate the average score for each category, incorporating input from all team members. 4. Use Scores to Guide Discussions: Leverage the scores to identify strengths and challenges, facilitating informed discussions about the implementation process. 5. Assess Capacity: Evaluate the capacity for implementation at all levels of the health system. This includes ensuring adequate staffing, administrative policies, and that personnel meet minimum qualifications to support the implementation of MEC/SPR. Capacity-building efforts should aim to improve and sustain local implementation. 6. Evaluate Fit: Conduct an analysis of community and regional priorities to confirm alignment with MEC/SPR recommendations. Additionally, assess the dissemination and integration of current family planning protocols within the community. 7. Assess Readiness: Determine the capacity of qualified implementation teams and their readiness to expand capacity for widespread implementation. This requires the presence of implementation drivers across multiple settings, technical expertise, and readily available tools for local adaptation. 8. Identify Needs: Evaluate how MEC/SPR can address the needs of current family planning systems at the country, community, and organizational levels. This assessment can be informed by existing data and evaluations. 9. Examine Evidence: Define the expected outcomes of implementing MEC/SPR and, if necessary, establish systems to monitor and assess these outcomes. Relevant outcomes may include contraceptive method mix and prevalence, unintended pregnancy rates, and associated costs (e.g., contraceptive use and pregnancy care). Review existing monitoring and evaluation systems for family planning activities and related systems that can serve as examples. Additionally, assess the availability of training, coaching, supervision resources, and expertise in family planning, as well as current communication mechanisms for data sharing and feedback. How to Use the Tool: The Readiness Assessment Tool evaluates six domains: Needs, Readiness, Fit, Evidence, Resources, and Capacity. Each domain is rated on a 5-point scale, where 5 indicates high readiness, 3 indicates medium readiness, and 1 indicates low readiness. The tool helps determine whether the available resources and systems at various levels (country, region, or clinic) are suitable for MEC/SPR implementation. It also assesses how well MEC/SPR recommendations align with current guidelines, protocols, and community priorities, and evaluates the capacity of implementation teams to support widespread adoption.
